D1.name: scene scratch
D1.lifecycle: ClearSceneState zeroes flags $0000-$000F at every scene load: STX $eventFlags with X = $0000 (16-bit, ROM bytes a2 00 00 / 8e 00 0a at 253273 / 253291) writes bytes $0A00-$0A01; its single call site is ExecuteSceneTransition (252507). OpenInventoryScreen pushes the same word, zeroes it for the overlay (the overlay exit flag is flag $0000) and pops it on close (191788-192094). The bytes are inside the save block, so a save and a load carry them, but the next scene load zeroes them again. The same index means different things in different scenes. A few scripts read the bytes as a whole: ir1F_plate_gate_opener (bits 1-4 of $0A00), mu66_rama_spirits (the $0A00 low byte equals $FE) and dm3F_switch / dm3F_mine_collapse_trigger (byte $0A01 used as a laborer counter). Verified at runtime: ClearSceneState zeroes exactly $0A00-$0A01 (flags $0000-$000F) once per scene load and leaves $0A02 and up, the kill block included, unchanged; the inventory overlay (scene $FF) zeroes the word on open and restores the saved word on close, with flag $FF cleared on open and set two frames after the close. Only quick warps were run: natural door exits and other scene-load callers were not traced.
D1.access: COP $CC-$D3 (byte and word forms), SetFlagRaw/TestFlagRaw/ClearFlagRaw, direct LDA/STA $eventFlags and $0A01.

D2.name: story / world events
D2.lifecycle: Part of the save block $0A00-$0BFB. Scripts set them, and a few scripts clear them (for example $96, $F4); no scene load clears a D2 bit except flag $FF (bit 7 of $0A1F), which ClearSceneState and the inventory overlay clear and set again after setup.
D2.access: COP flag opcodes, the *Raw helpers (actor-parameter indices: laborers $A0-$A3, necklace stones $98/$99, statues $F8-$FD, orbs $F2/$F3), scene-meta gates (D9).

D3.name: event triggers / death actions
D3.lifecycle: Bytes $0A20-$0A3F of the save block. ApplyAllEventBlocks (scene load, after InitCameraBounds and before SpawnSceneActors, and at inventory close) walks all 256 bits; a set flag $0100+n applies event block n when the block's scene byte equals sceneCurrent. Scene loads never clear these bits. The only clear sites are the sg52 blockers ($0125-$012A), the Ishtar room controller ($0149-$0150 at each room start), the Adrift script ($0120), the stone coffin retry ($013B), Kara's return ($0119) and the prologue ($017C-$017F). Blocks n >= 158 have no table entry (LookupEventBlock does not bound the index); no flag in $019E-$01FF has a setter.
D3.access: COP word forms ($CD/$CF/$D1/$D3 and the Branch/Wait variants), SetFlag_0100/TestFlag_0100 (death-action indices, pyCC Dark Space portal), ApplyAllEventBlocks (LDA $0A20,Y), enemy-spawn rows of tables/scene_actors.asm (last operand = event-block index, stored at $7F0024).

D4.name: chests and hidden Red Jewels
D4.lifecycle: Bytes $0A40-$0A5F of the save block; no scene load, world-map entry or game over clears them (ClearSceneState zeroes only $0A00-$0A01, ClearAllWramFlags only $0A80-$0A9F) and no clear wrapper exists for the _0200 base, so a set bit stays for the life of the save. Chests use $0201-$022E (the record byte AND $7F, so the table can address only $0200-$027F); hidden Red Jewels use $0280-$028F (actor attribute >> 1 plus $80); the two ranges cannot collide. The other 194 indices have no reader and no writer.
D4.access: TestEventFlag_0200 (PlaceOpenedChestTiles, RadarPlotSceneMarkers, HiddenRedJewelInteract) and SetEventFlag_0200 (HandleChestInteraction twice, HiddenRedJewelInteract); no COP literal, no direct byte access and no other helper reaches $0200-$02FF.

D5.name: scene clear reward
D5.lifecycle: Bytes $0A60-$0A7F of the save block; ClearSceneState zeroes only $0A00-$0A01 and ClearAllWramFlags only $0A80-$0A9F, and no clear wrapper exists for the _0300 base, so a set bit stays for the life of the save. Flag $0300 + scene id marks the stat reward of that scene as claimed. Only the 87 scenes with a nonzero enemy_clear_reward_table tier ever get the bit; the other 169 indices are never written.
D5.access: TestFlag_0300 (RadarScreenSetup, StandardEnemyDefeatHandler twice, field_reveal_object, BossClearApplyStatReward) and SetFlag_0300 (RewardActorVFX, BossClearApplyStatReward); no COP operand, no direct byte access and no other helper reaches $0300-$03FF.

D6.name: dungeon enemy kill
D6.lifecycle: Bytes $0A80-$0A9F of the save block (flag $0400 + enemy number; byte $0A80 + (n >> 3), bit n AND 7). Zeroed by ClearAllWramFlags (WorldMapController entry {238336}, st68_kara {438261}, sp58_red_eye {426502} only when $0AA6 = 2), by the inline loop of game_over_sequence {54988}-{55002} on a real game over (gems < 100; a revive keeps the bits) and at boot. ClearSceneState zeroes only $0A00-$0A01, so ordinary scene changes keep the bits: a number reused by two scenes of one visit is one shared bit, and a number reused by the next dungeon is a stale bit unless a reset ran between the dungeons. Each dungeon numbers its enemies from about $01, so 241 of the 253 numbers appear in several scenes. Verified at runtime: ordinary scene loads keep the kill block $0A80-$0A9F; the clearing sites (world-map entry, revive, game over, save/load) were not run.
D6.access: COP $D8 SetDungeonKillFlag (StandardEnemyDefeatHandler {56306}, EnemyDefeatDispatch {697510}, awB1_wall_walker {770381}, pyCC_mystic_ball {771937}; all reach SetWramFlag {44172}), CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag at spawn ({249721}), one direct reader (gw88_tomb_dark_space {507380}, $0A9F) and the two clearing sites. No COP flag operand and no other helper call reaches $0400-$04FF.

D7.name: boss reward / ability unlock
D7.lifecycle: Byte $0AA0 (flags $0500-$0507) and the word $0AA2-$0AA3 (flags $0510-$051F, also abilityBitmask) lie in the save block $0A00-$0BFB. ClearSceneState zeroes only $0A00-$0A01; ClearAllWramFlags (WorldMapController {238336}, st68_kara {438261}, sp58_red_eye {426502}) and the inline loop of game_over_sequence ({54988}-{55002}) zero exactly $0A80-$0A9F, one byte below $0AA0, so a set bit survives scene changes, the world map and a game over. Boot zero-fills WRAM and SystemInit clears the low byte of abilityBitmask again ({32946}); DiaryNewGameStart writes neither byte (FL10), so a new game starts from the boot zeros. The range shipped for D7 is narrowed to the 8 + 16 bits that have storage: $0508-$050F ($0AA1) is unassigned and $0520-$059F is not flag storage ($0AA4-$0AB3 hold state words, FL10 byte map).
D7.access: Boss flags: TestWramFlag_Offset100 / SetWramFlag_Offset100 (index AND 7, base $0100 on wramFlags $0A80), called by boss_clear_reward_handler ({49883}, {49928}) and tested at spawn by the six lair actors ({695049}, {708981}, {717345}, {717790}, {754027}, {763580}). Ability flags: TestFlag_0510 (+$0510, one call: TestAbilityFlag {190952}) and direct 16-bit access of abilityBitmask $0AA2 (31 inventory rows in 8 files: one live setter, sE6_gaia AbilityOrbActor {584379}/{584382}). No COP flag operand, no scene-meta gate and no other helper reaches $0500-$051F.

D8.name: non-bitfield gates
D8.lifecycle: Items, character form, gems and other bytes of the save block that scripts test (FL40 extends the tool). Four 16-bit state words sit inside the flag-array tail: $0AA6 (script state: SwitchCase selector in dc2F_adrift, plate id in UseItem plate handlers), $0AAC globalScriptIndex (Dark Space layout variant, hieroglyph slot index), $0AB0 jewelsCollected, $0AB2 (Dark Space layout variant, saved copy of $0AAC).
D8.access: COP $D4-$D7 (items), SwitchCase on $0AD4/$0AA6, direct reads and writes.

D9.name: scene-meta gates
D9.lifecycle: A flag index read from a scene-meta command stream (SceneCmd_Branch, opcode $13 <flag> <label>) at scene load. TestFlagRaw masks the index to a byte, so only flags $0000-$00FF can gate. The 18 gates of 11 records use nine indices, all D2: $21, $4C, $70, $7B, $7E, $88, $96, $B3, $F4. A set flag skips to the unique $14 label (possibly in another record); a clear flag continues with the next command.

meanings.summary: Scratch bits $08-$0F are read as the single byte $0A01: a hit counter. Each of the four dm3F_switch placements zeroes it at spawn and adds 1 per hit; dm3F_mine_collapse_trigger fires when the byte equals 4.

runtime.trial: FL24-01a set: Byte $0A01 of scene $3F is incremented (INC at 381015) by a real sword hit (physical B) on a dm3F_switch: three different switches gave $0A01 = 1, 2, 3. With $0A01 := 3 ... | clear: Not cleared after spawn; zeroed by the STZ at spawn (not exercised separately).

meanings.notes: The counter does not track freed laborers: hits on any of the four switches (scene_actors ;1D-;20 of scene 63) increase it, and each spawn of a switch resets it, so a later-spawned switch placement would restart the count. hit_switch with a type byte of 10 or more would also write these bits; no such placement exists in scene 63. The flag word $0121 latches the collapse. FR22: FR22_20261105.md FL24-01 (raw/FR22_FL24-01_R5, M1, M2).

meanings.name: sys_scene_setup_done
meanings.summary: The scene's palette buffer, PPU registers and HDMA tables are set up: ClearSceneState clears the flag before it rebuilds the scene, the scene-start sequence sets it after its two thinker passes, and the inventory overlay clears it at open and sets it after the first render frame of its close path. Thinkers that own palette or HDMA state re-apply it in every pass that finds the flag clear.

effects.set: The HDMA and PPU-register thinkers (sine_hdma_slow_wave, sine_hdma_ending_wave, sine_hdma_dual_channel, native_village_sine_hdma, dao_sine_hdma_slow, larai_cliff_scroll_wave, palace_coffin_hdma_table, mu_tint_and_wave, comet_lair_hdma_a/b/c_timed, sE8_comet_display_config) continue their per-frame tick; palace_fountain_palette keeps cycling; the palette loops that wait for a clear flag (edward_castle_alarm_palette, dream_palette_loop, flag_gated_palette_cool/warm, gold_ship_wreck_palette) stay parked.
effects.clear: The HDMA and PPU-register thinkers jump back to their init label and rewrite their tables or registers; palace_fountain_palette sets the flag again and rewrites CGADSUB; the parked palette loops resume, replay their bundle and set the flag again.

evidence: extracted/system/engine/scene_lifecycle.asm:844 {253423} (write that clears bit 7: the direct clear at the top of ClearSceneState)
extracted/system/inventory/inventory_overlay.asm:133 {191819} (write that clears bit 7: the direct clear at open)

runtime.trial: FL10-04 set: ClearSceneState sets the latch with COP SetFlagByte #FF (offset 253564) in the same frame as the helper store (f=563 in scenes $15 and $24, f=447 in scene $08); the ... | clear: ClearSceneState clears it at offset 253423 (f=395) and the inventory open at offset 191819; clear windows measured: 168 frames ($15, $24), 52 frames ($08), 65 frames ...; FL21-05 scene $0A set: The alarm thinker (offsets 46643, 46655, 46674, 46677) runs only with $21 set and $22 clear (otherwise it reaches the kill at 46683 on its first frame). It runs ...; FL22-10 scene $1D set: larai_cliff_scroll_wave sets $FF at offset 48543 in the first frames of scene $1D (bit set at frame 1 of the settle). | clear: Clearing the bit at settle frames 100 and 160 re-runs the setup (48543 count 1 > 3, HDMA enable $66 toggles $06 > $0E > $06 one frame later); the BranchOnFlagByte at ...; FL23-08 scene $2A set: dream_palette_loop sets $FF once (offset 46809; the bit is already set at the first settle sample of scene $2A) and parks in WaitOnFlagByte #FF,#00 (46812 polled 724 ... | clear: Clearing the bit at settle frames 250 and 450 restarts bundle #35 (46804 count 1 > 2 > 3) and sets the bit again within 1 frame; KillThinker (46818) never ran. The ...; FL25-04 set: $FF (byte $0A1F bit 7) is already set at the first sample after the arrival in scenes $5F, $60, $5C and $5D; in $5F and $60 the tint thinker passes its flag test once ... | clear: No clear observed.; FL28-12 set: Set by the engine (value 1 at the end of the load); the sine HDMA init entry (48884 / 48851) runs once (frame 543 / 551) and the tick bodies (48898, 48904 / 48865 ... | clear: Clearing $FF after the load re-runs the init entry repeatedly (48884: frames 543 to 712; 48851: 551 to 713) and the tick bodies stop (48904 last at frame 631; 48871 last ...; FL29-11 set: The engine sets $FF at load; the display config 846710 and the HDMA init 48452 run once (frame 458) and the tick body 48478 runs every frame from 462 on | clear: Clearing $FF after the load re-runs the display config (846710: frames 458 to 580) and the HDMA init (48452: frames 458 to 626) repeatedly and the tick body 48478 stops ...; FL10-04 set: Bit 7 of $0A1F is set after a scene load (arrival) and again after the inventory overlay closes. | clear: Cleared while the overlay is open (byte $00 with the overlay in scene $FF). The palette replay half is not run.

meanings.notes: One flag with one meaning, not an idiom. The protocol: (1) only the engine clears it, at two sites that are direct writes, not COP clears (the inventory has 0 ClearFlagByte/ClearFlagWord sites with operand $FF, and its direct_accesses list writes of $0A00-$0A3F only at those two places, besides the flag helpers, which take a computed index, and save_system, which copies the whole array; ClearEventFlag is called only by the COP handlers, ClearFlagRaw only by ir1F_gold_tile with indices 1-4); (2) the engine sets it at {253564} (scene setup) and {192190} (overlay close); (3) thinkers that own state which the rebuild destroys test it: pattern A (12 placed thinker files and the unplaced native_village_dup_unused: init, SetEntryHereAndYield, branch back to init while the flag is clear) re-initialises HDMA tables or PPU registers; pattern B (5 placed palette loops and the unplaced palette_buffer_clear_unused: set the flag themselves, then WaitOnFlagByte(FF, clear)) replay their palette bundle; palace_fountain_palette is a hybrid (it sets the flag, cycles, and sets it again when it finds it clear). Pattern B cannot be woken by a scene setup: the scene's thinker list is built by SpawnSceneThinkers after the clear at {253418}, and the scene-start passes at {253549}/{253553} come before the set at {253564}. It wakes once per inventory close: RestoreGameState restores the saved thinker list, ResetThinkerWaitCounters (inventory_overlay.asm:295, called at {192179}) zeroes the wait counters, and the first UpdateFrameRender at {192186} runs RunThinkers_Hdma_Light and RunThinkers_General_Light while $FF is still clear (the overlay's eventFlags restore at {192094} covers flags $00-$0F only); the set at {192190} comes after that frame. The shipped thinker notes say 'next scene setup or inventory open': the first half is wrong, the second is the close path (specs/FL31_notes.json). Self-sets by thinkers (12 sites: 2 engine and 10 in thinker files, 9 of them placed) cannot hide a clear from a later thinker of the same pass: the only scenes in which one file sets and another file tests are $5C (palace_coffin_hdma_table sets, sine_hdma_dual_channel tests; thinker_spawn_0CE96F lists the coffin thinker first) and $E8 (testers only). The coffin thinker sets the flag one tick after its init (SetFlagByte at {48753} follows SetEntryHereAndYield), so in the pass that finds the flag clear it re-initialises without setting, and the engine's own set at {192190} (or {253564} at scene setup) comes before its next tick. Two thinkers in unused/ (native_village_dup_unused, palette_buffer_clear_unused) are referenced by no scene thinker list. FR00: FR00_20261104.md, Verdicts row FL10-04 (thinker half): no gated palette or HDMA thinker was observed across a clear and a set.

effects.set: InitActorFromSceneData frees the slot of every enemy spawn record with this number (CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag carry set), does not count it in enemiesRemaining and swaps the record's event-block tiles
effects.clear: Every spawn record with this number spawns its actor normally and the actor is counted in enemiesRemaining.

effects.set: InitActorFromSceneData frees the slot of every enemy spawn record with this number (CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag carry set), does not count it in enemiesRemaining and swaps the record's event-block tiles
effects.clear: Every spawn record with this number spawns its actor normally and the actor is counted in enemiesRemaining.

meanings.notes: Rows: $26#06 ir1B_slugger; $45#05 dm3D_grundit; $50#08 sg4D_cyber.sg4D_red_cyber; $62#08 sp5C_slipper; $A4#06 mtA0_skulker.mtA0_skulker_ew; $B5#0C awB1_wall_walker.awB1_wall_walker4; $D3#06 pyD2_haunt. The number is used in 7 dungeon session(s) (warp-graph components of the scenes with tracked numbers: $1D $3D $4D $5F $A0 $B0 $CC); a reset runs only at world-map entry, st68_kara, sp58_red_eye and game over, so same-number rows of different sessions share one bit unless one of those intervenes. Full record because: own-D8 actor row, actor that may skip or never write the bit. awB1_wall_walker: boss-bit branch (OrExtraFlags #$0080 at awB1_wall_walker.asm:128 {769087} and :185 {769211}) makes StandardEnemyDefeatHandler skip the kill bit; the own death routine (:526 {770381}) sets it on every non-last kill. pyD2_haunt: OrExtraFlags #$0090 (pyD2_haunt.asm:211 {770788}) includes the boss bit $0080, so the StandardEnemyDefeatHandler path skips the kill bit. The name is a slot name (enemy number), not derived from dialog text.
